audience.programmeDescription: Delft’s Systems Engineering, Policy Analysis & Management bachelor examines technological systems together with the people, institutions and policies that govern them. It combines engineering analysis, mathematical and computational methods, economics, law and governance. Students choose a technology domain; the curriculum shown follows Energy & Industry.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The energy option combines actual energy-system study with quantitative methods and public policy. The data option shifts the technical emphasis to computing, data analysis and digital systems, retaining law, economics and policy. Both offer substantive related study, with different specialist coverage and project requirements from Delft.

curriculum.limitation: Dutch full-time bachelor. Later years follow the nominal structure for this entrant cohort. The 30-EC minor remains open within approved options.

componentNotes.tb-minor: Year 3, first semester. Approved 30-EC minor; no particular package is prescribed here. Individual packages require examination-board approval and must satisfy level and overlap rules.
componentNotes.TB351D: Year 3, ordinary Q3–Q4 start: one 15-EC independent final project, not two projects. All first-year courses must be passed and no more than one 5-EC second-year module may remain. Timely registration is compulsory.
componentNotes.TB241EA: Year 2. Physical heat, mass and momentum transfer; this is not transport or logistics planning.

cellNotes.text: Technical and economic assessment of energy demand and solar, wind and bioenergy options; not the full industrial-process sequence.
Statistical learning on real data; public-policy datasets or projects are not guaranteed.

concepts.label: Energy systems, modelling & public policy
concepts.concept: A programme combining energy resources, conversion and renewable-system design with mathematical modelling, probability, numerical methods and optimisation. Economics, law, qualitative research, EU policymaking, public-policy analysis and sustainability governance connect technological choices with public decisions and competing interests. Climate science and life-cycle assessment support evaluation of energy transitions. It provides a substantive interdisciplinary response to the Energy & Industry direction, with gaps in industrial-process engineering, agent-based and system-dynamics simulation, specialist infrastructure economics and safety, and Delft’s compulsory final project.

concepts.label: Data systems, decision methods & public policy
concepts.concept: A programme centred on programming, software, databases and digital networks, supported by statistical learning, algorithms, probability, numerical methods and optimisation. Law, economics, public-policy analysis, AI ethics and organisational research address the institutional and social decisions surrounding digital systems. Its priority is computational analysis and the governance of digital change, rather than energy technology. Technical projects are not guaranteed to concern public policy; the programme does not reproduce Delft’s full engineering-and-policy sequence or its compulsory final project.
